all_findings.issue: spec_text_vs_execution_drift: AC6 in acceptance-criteria JSON says 'process.exit(0) is NOT called' (negative pattern check) and check.negative_pattern='process.exit'. BA spec ticket AC6 says 'process.exit(1) is called (not 0, not omitted); a FATAL log message is emitted'. These are different literal formulations. The JSON negative check would pass even if process.exit(2) were called; the BA spec positive check requires specifically process.exit(1). BA must update AC6 in acceptance-criteria JSON to match the BA spec literal: check.pattern='process.exit(1)' (positive) not negative_pattern='process.exit'.
all_findings.recommendation: BA should update acceptance-criteria-20260525-081012.json AC6 check to use pattern='process.exit(1)' positive check AND assert FATAL log message present, matching the BA spec ticket literal text.

all_findings.issue: scope_alignment gap: test_AC4 checks only cleanupAndShutdown (Site 2). BA spec AC4 requires checking heartbeat handoff site (Site 1, run.ts ~763-766). The acceptance-criteria JSON AC4 also only specifies cleanupAndShutdown, meaning both the test and the JSON share this scope gap. The heartbeat handoff site was verified by QA direct inspection only, not by generated test. If either spec or test is authoritative, a test covering both sites should exist.
all_findings.recommendation: BA should extend AC4 in acceptance-criteria JSON to cover both sites, and dev should extend test_AC4 to check both run.ts heartbeat handoff block and cleanupAndShutdown. This is a test-coverage gap, not a code defect (code passes at both sites).
